entries.title: Centered two-arm finite geodesic certificate
entries.statement: For a finite nonnegative edge-weight field on nearest-neighbor Z^2, H_m(v) is the event that there is a self-avoiding finite path (z_-m,...,z_m) with z_0=v, consecutive vertices adjacent, and total cost equal to the infimum over ALL finite lattice paths between z_-m and z_m. The two arms each have m edges. Minimize in the entire lattice; confined shortest paths are not this certificate.
assumptions: global minimization and simple path witnesses

entries.title: DRAFT P0117: stationary boundary-geodesic occupation density
entries.statement: AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT for P0117; w392 independent audit pending; no novelty or solution claim. For stationary measurable finite nonnegative edge weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, let B_n=[-n,n]^2 intersect Z^2, A be the vertices on self-avoiding bigeodesics, and D_n be the vertices in B_n on ANY self-avoiding globally minimizing finite path with endpoints on the vertex boundary of B_2n. Paths may leave B_2n, and all geodesics are included if ties occur. Let H_n(0) mean existence of a self-avoiding globally minimizing path (z_-n,...,z_n) with z_0=0 and adjacent consecutive vertices. Then P(0 in A)<=E|D_n|/|B_n|<=P(H_n(0)). Centered-prefix compactness gives P(H_n(0)) decreasing to P(0 in A); hence the expected occupation density tends to P(0 in A). Almost-sure absence of ALL bigeodesics is equivalent to E|D_n|=o(n^2). This iid decay estimate is not proved here.
assumptions: union over all finite geodesics with the specified endpoints

entries.title: DRAFT P0117 audit scar: an infinite ray must cross every shell
entries.statement: AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT for P0117; w392 independent audit pending. Let T_0 be the union of all infinite simple nearest-neighbor paths from 0 in Z^2 whose every finite segment globally minimizes passage time, q(x)=P(x in T_0), and S_n={x:||x||_infinity=n}. Every such ray hits S_n, so sum_{x in S_n}q(x)=E|T_0 intersect S_n|>=P(T_0 nonempty). If a ray exists almost surely, the sum is at least 1 for every n and sup_{x in S_n}q(x)>=1/(8n). Thus vanishing raw forward-ray shell incidence and the uniform rate o(1/n) are impossible in this setting. This concerns forward rays and does not imply a bigeodesic exists.
assumptions: P(T_0 nonempty)=1 for the numerical lower bound 1

entries.title: REFUTED closing step: make forward-ray shell incidence vanish
entries.statement: AUTHOR-CHECKED AUDIT SCAR; w392 independent review pending; not a theorem proving absence. A proposed route defines T_x as the union of all infinite geodesic rays from x and uses the valid stationary inequality P(bigeodesic through 0)<=one-half times sum_{x in S_n}P(-x in T_0). Its proposed closing estimate, that this raw shell sum vanishes along a subsequence or that the shell maximum is o(1/n), is unattainable whenever a ray exists from 0 almost surely: every ray crosses every surrounding shell and the sum is always at least 1. Keep the counting inequality; replace the closing quantity by genuinely two-sided extension witnesses or full boundary-geodesic occupation. The parent P0117 conjecture remains unresolved in this packet.
assumptions: S_n is the vertex boundary of [-n,n]^2

relations.rationale: The density sandwich uses centered globally minimizing simple paths; a finitely branching prefix tree identifies their intersection with a bigeodesic through the center. Author-checked draft; independent audit pending.

The lower-bound card gives shell sum >=1 when a ray exists almost surely. The refuted route proposes that exactly this raw forward-ray shell sum tend to zero. These two numerical assertions are incompatible. Independent audit pending.

Occupation by all long boundary-to-boundary finite geodesics is an attainable equivalent target for bigeodesic absence, while the raw forward-ray shell sum cannot vanish. No proof of occupation decay is supplied.

The existing P0117 concept asks for absence of bi-infinite geodesics under continuous iid planar weights. This stationary occupation reduction expresses that absence as a precise subquadratic expected occupation estimate without importing an unproved directional regularity condition.

The existing attempt warns that unanchored opposite-endpoint geodesics can escape each fixed ball. The certificate explicitly requires the center and two arms of growing length, which supplies an anchor for compactness; it does not show such certificates occur or disappear.
